validator_result: OK (exit 0, no ERROR lines). Five ATYPICAL lines concern our units, and each is recorded in that unit's atypical list under its exact rule string, with a note. Anna: 'availability:unique min_tier t2', 'bodies:humanoid allowed.aim-models auto-target', 'weapon-families:sniper allowed.target-types structure' and 'weapon-traits:stun min_tier t2'. Olga: 'availability:unique min_tier t2'. The WARN lines about our units are the expected kinds: fire-power-shot and cloak are planned patterns, and the source_units of repair-allies, throw-explosive and transform are out of date until the merge pass runs sync-patterns. The file did not exist before, so I created it with the given header, and it holds only these two units.
copy_check_result: Exit 0. I ran `node scripts/copy-check.mjs . --only wiki/Anna_Kos --only wiki/Wojtek --only article/116 --only article/106 --only article/110 --only wiki/Olga_Romanova --only wiki/Changa --only article/92 --only article/94 --only article/117`. All 10 cited pages were checked from the cache, none were left unchecked, and it found no shared runs. The first run found 7 shared runs of 6 to 10 words, in four source notes and two uncertain notes, copied from Change Log #20, Change Log #17, DevBlog #40, Change Log #04 and the Anna Kos page. I rewrote them and the run then passed. I also checked every prose string of both units against all 185 Iron Harvest pages I read, uncited ones included: wiki pages, KING Art posts 67 to 123 and the Steam news feed. That check found no runs of 6 or more words apart from URL fragments. I also reworded the 5-word near-quotes; only the wiki's unit-type label 'Infantry Support Hero' is left. No PDF is cited.

hesitations.reason: Step 4 counts official text that says the unit is strong against a target. I read DevBlog #40 (Changelog 23), which says the pair beats most early infantry groups, as that kind of text. The registry's list of strong-against lines read so far does not include it, and it is a balance comparison rather than a matchup line. Without it, steps 1 to 4 give nothing, and step 5 gives assault (her speed is medium, so not raider).

Change Log #20 says Wojtek now heals allied infantry. I read 'heals' as a word form of the alias healer, as the vocabulary allows ('harasses' for harasser). Read strictly, the post does not call the unit a healer. The heal is a passive, not a button, mode or weapon, so no other step would rank support.

hesitations.chosen: disabler at step 3, through the rifle's stun trait
hesitations.reason: The rule is clear, but it stands on one wiki sentence, that soldiers who survive her shot are knocked down and left exposed (see armament/0/traits).

The registry says DevBlog #40's 'sniper' names marksman. But marksman requires a sniper weapon that reaches long, and her rifle reaches 32 against the reference rifle's 23, a ratio of 1.39, which is medium. The rule is clear, but she sits close to the 1.5 edge, the reach figure dates from 2020, and the wiki calls her reach the best of the infantry heroes.

Scout's requirements fail: medium speed, sight is only a proposal, and she has no sensor, stealth, mark or reveal. The wiki's 'specializes in scouting' and the Unit page's 'great scouts' are the wiki's own words, which the roles rules do not read.
The registry note settles this: heroes arrive only through a reserve, and DevBlog #40 puts the pair in Reserve 1. Because unique availability starts at t2, this is recorded as atypical.
The registry note says to use iron + 3 × oil from the infobox, with an uncertain entry. No page says what that price buys, and since DevBlog #35 a reserve's price depends on what it holds.

The wiki says surviving soldiers are knocked down and left vulnerable. Stun means the target can't act for a very short time, while knockback means it is pushed away. No source gives a duration. Knockdowns may be a general reaction of soldiers to heavy hits (the Kolokol knocks Anna down; DevBlog #40 stops retreating infantry from tumbling). Stun also brings an atypical (its floor is t2) and gives the disabler role.
The ratio of 1.39 is below 1.5, so the rule is clear. The source is weaker: the figure was entered in September 2020 and no post confirms it.
No source says how the round travels, so the delivery rule gives the family default.

alternatives: leave out structure (the sniper family excludes it)
hesitations.reason: The infobox's damage figure against buildings counts as a source saying the weapon damages buildings, so structure is listed and recorded as atypical. Air is left out because no source says the rifle attacks air units (registry: air reach is not game-wide).

hesitations.chosen: Wojtek's Ferocious Maul as a secondary blades weapon
alternatives: leave it out under the game-wide Melee note
describe it only inside the companion ability
hesitations.reason: The registry note leaves out only the plain melee blow every squad has, and keeps a melee weapon the unit is built around. The infobox lists the maul as her second weapon slot ('Wojtek's Melee'), and the bear fights mainly with it. It is missing while he waits to respawn.

In the aim tie-break, step 2 (fires by itself while the player does something else, like drones acting on their own) comes before step 4 (a creature carries it: free-aim). This gives the atypical humanoid + auto-target.
It rests on one wiki line, a simile about him scattering soldiers.
One body plan cannot describe a soldier with a bear partner. I recorded this as a fit_note.
The count is 'bodies per purchase'. The bear has his own health and is always summoned, but he is no squad member, and the rules do not say whether a companion counts as a body.
The size describes the plan's body, Anna. The bear also vaults walls like infantry (DevBlog #24).
Squad needs soldiers or tiny drones that move as one with a shared fate. Wojtek acts alone, can be sent away, and kept fighting after she fell (Change Log #17).

hesitations.chosen: empty, with a fit_note for command-companion
hesitations.reason: Under the pattern-link test, reinforce-squad's follower variant matches only the bear's return after a wait. The autonomous partner that obeys send and recall orders is not covered by any pattern. launch-drones is for expendable minions released on a key.

The sources disagree: the Anna Kos page says he heals all nearby infantry over time, while the Wojtek page says one unit at a time, out of combat. I marked this sources_disagree; the kind and pattern hold either way.
The registry's game-wide note is clear. But the model's own definition (the unit can crawl, and an enemy can finish it) does not match Iron Harvest heroes, so the differences are in armour.notes.
The downed state is coded as an armour model, and a hero is never removed in skirmish or multiplayer. No on-death term describes 'never removed', and wreck is barred for organic units.
The wiki's Pros praise her field of view in words only. Under the sight rule, words do not change the band.

hesitations.chosen: armour-class:>=medium, unit:iron-harvest.rusviet.kolokol, weapon:flamethrower; massed infantry left out
hesitations.reason: Matchups rule 6: DevBlog #40 has the pair beat most infantry groups, while the wiki says she stands little chance against large numbers, so infantry is left out with a sources_disagree entry. hesitations.reason: availability:unique would also cover the tier 2 mech heroes, for whom the reason is false (Matchups rule 1).
No source names this pairing. It is reasoned from the wiki's Cons, and I added an uncertain entry.
Each scores only 1 point, and step 3 needs 2.
The cited official pages are patch notes, which do not count toward high, and both wiki pages are one site.

No source names her reserve. The registry note says to take the band the evidence best supports: Change Log #04 groups her with Anna and Gunter as infantry heroes, and both of them come with Reserve I.

No source gives a price, and no rule says how to band a unit with no price. I judged it from the other foot, horse and exosuit heroes' wiki prices: Anna very low; Gunter, Michał Sikorski and Victor Popov low.

Under the speed comparison rule, 'can outrun regular infantry' gives the reference unit's band unless the source says much faster. The bare word 'fast' only goes in notes. This choice decides between raider and assault.

Step 1: 'assassin' (Change Log #06) is no role label or alias. Step 2 is skipped because the gun does damage. Steps 3 and 4 find nothing, so step 5 applies and depends on the speed band. Infiltrator comes from no step, and the tie-break sends charges to an anti role.

Anti-infantry rests on reading Change Log #04's halved light-armour damage as 'small arms that do little to vehicles'; there is no unarmoured figure to compare. Anti-armour fails its requirements, and step 2 gives it only for a bonus, a label or a single-target button. Her charges also hit buildings and soldiers.

Ground vehicles rest on Change Log #04's light-armour figure. Structures are filled in by can_target step 4, because no source speaks of the gun and buildings.
She plants the charge on a chosen target, so it is not a mine. Going off when she walks out of range is a twist on the remote charge.

unclear_rules.note: It is unclear whether a verb describing what the unit does (Change Log #20: Wojtek 'heals' allied infantry) counts as calling the unit by an alias (healer), the way 'harasses' counts for harasser. This decides Anna's support role, because a passive heal ranks at no other roles.secondary step. A support hero whose healing is passive therefore loses support unless official text names it.

DevBlog #40 says the pair has 'the edge over most groups of infantry'. The rules do not say whether a balance comparison like this counts as official text that the unit is strong against a target (roles.primary step 4). The registry's list of strong-against lines does not include it.

No rule covers a purchase that is a soldier plus a separate AI animal. The open questions are body.count (counted or not), the body plan (only one shape), the crew model (solo vs squad), whether the animal's attack is a weapon of the unit (the bear's maul is the infobox's second slot), and its mount (auto-target breaks the humanoid plan). The trim proposes command-companion as a new pattern for both.

The registry puts the knock-out in armour.models (downed-revive) and leaves on_death to the 3C default, respawn. Respawn means 'simply gone', but an Iron Harvest hero is never removed. No on-death term fits, and downed-revive's own definition (crawling, enemies can finish it) differs too.

unclear_rules.topic: Stealth sensor trait vs cloak pattern
unclear_rules.note: Olga is invisible until an enemy is within about half its range. That matches the stealth trait's text ('enemies see it only at close range'), but the trait's note sends full invisibility to cloak. The registry allows either, so two coders could split here.

unclear_rules.topic: Body plan and size of a ridden mode
unclear_rules.note: It is unclear whether a rider on a big cat is a new upper-body shape (beast) and whether size changes when the game still treats the rider as infantry.

The Melee note leaves out the plain blow every squad has but keeps weapons a unit is built around. A hero whose sabre the wiki calls her secondary weapon, and whose melee damage KING Art retunes, falls between the two.

unclear_rules.topic: Behaviour described only inside another ability
unclear_rules.note: It is unclear whether Changa fighting briefly after a dismount, described only in the Ride the Tiger text but tuned in the posts, meets the 'distinct state or behaviour' bar for its own triggered entry.

Stun's floor is t2 and its meaning mentions a medium or longer cooldown, yet Anna's basic rifle knocks soldiers down on any hit. Knockdowns may be a game-wide reaction of soldiers to heavy hits, which the game-wide mechanics list does not cover.

unclear_rules.topic: Banding a price no source gives
unclear_rules.note: Speed has a rule for 'nothing usable' (judge from neighbouring units, with an uncertain entry), but cost_band has none. I used the same method for Olga.

unclear_rules.topic: What a hero's infobox price buys
unclear_rules.note: The registry says to use iron + 3 × oil with an uncertain entry. Heroes are picked for reserve coins and called in with a reserve whose price depends on its contents (DevBlog #35), so the raw figure's meaning is unknown.

new_mechanics.summary: A lasting AI partner, here a bear, stays with the hero, fights on its own once engaged, and takes short orders (attack a target, come back); it has its own health, can draw fire or heal allies, and comes back after a long wait if killed. Counterplay: focus or burn the companion down (flamers, massed infantry), then strike the fragile hero during the respawn wait, or kite the companion away from its master.

The same lasting AI partner, here a tiger that stays hidden, comes when called to serve as a mount, and fights beside the hero for a short time after an attack ends the ride, with its own health and a respawn cooldown. Counterplay: catch the hero while she is mounted and visible, or kill the tiger to take away her escape for the length of its cooldown.

source_problems:
Olga has no figures anywhere I could read. Her wiki infobox gives only a unit type and Unarmored, and the page history shows it never had stats. The Russian wiki's stat table is blank, the archive wiki pages are stubs, and no KING Art post from 67 to 123 or Steam news item gives her price, speed or ability cooldowns. So her cost band and speed band are judgements: no cost raw, no speed raw. The brief asked for 'her price from the DevBlogs', but no DevBlog I read names one. Her reserve is not named by any source either, so t1 is the best-supported reading.

Anna's wiki infobox figures date from September 2020. Its damage to light armour predates Change Log #17's cut (marked sources_disagree). The Wojtek page calls the bear far tougher than Anna, while the posts cut his health to well below hers. The two wiki pages also disagree on how his heal works (all nearby units vs one at a time, out of combat).

The wiki titles Olga's page 'Olga Romanova' (displayed as Olga Morozova), and the ability is spelled 'Rider the Tiger' there. TV Tropes, which a search snippet said lists the infantry heroes as First Reserve, returned HTTP 403 and was not used. Both cited wiki pages were read through the MediaWiki API. All copy-check pages came from cache, with nothing left unchecked.
